_note: Built-in AI per browser (Nov 2026), consolidated from data/research/ai-*.json. level: 0 none, 1 basic chat/summaries, 2 integrated assistant, 3 agentic. quality 1-5 = how capable/well-regarded. Browsers not listed have no built-in AI. Channels inherit from their parent in browsers.ts.

aloha-browser.models: user-selectable models (unnamed), anonymized via Aloha's Private AI
aloha-browser.note: Private AI is a chat assistant with mixed, anonymized requests, a model picker and optional web search. It can't see your browsing, so it isn't tab-aware. Free use is limited to a few requests a day (Premium is unlimited), and all AI can be turned off. Desktop parity with mobile wasn't fully verified. AlohaJet, a separate agent-driven browser, isn't counted.

arc.note: Arc Max is an opt-in bundle: ChatGPT in the command bar, Ask on Page, 5-second link previews and tidy tab/download names, with little tab awareness. Arc is discontinued: no new accounts since Oct 22 2026, mobile AI off Nov 23, and the desktop app stops working Dec 22 2026.

ardia.models: none built in (bring your own Claude Code/Codex via the ardia CLI)
ardia.note: Ardia has no AI by design: its site says nothing in Ardia calls a model. Your own Claude Code or Codex can drive it through the ardia CLI, which is an external agent rather than built-in AI.

aside.models: your ChatGPT or Claude subscription, or your own API key
aside.note: This AI-first YC browser (June 2026) has an agent that works across your logged-in sites, with Ultrabrowse long runs, routines, on-device markdown memory, and a password manager that hides credentials from the AI. Payments, posts and messages wait for your confirmation. The free tier has limited credits and paid tiers add more. Early reviews call it promising but buggy and its benchmarks self-reported; no local model option is documented.

avast-secure-browser.models: undisclosed third-party providers via Avast privacy proxy
avast-secure-browser.note: The side panel (shown by default) includes Smart Chat, an AI chatbot that answers questions, polishes text and summarizes the current page. Requests go through a proxy that hides your IP. Avast doesn't name the model provider.

avg-secure-browser.models: undisclosed third-party providers (same Smart Chat as Avast)
avg-secure-browser.note: AVG's side panel, open on the right by default, has the same Smart Chat as Avast: an AI chatbot for questions, page summaries and image generation.

avira-secure-browser.note: Unlike its Avast, AVG and Norton siblings, I found no Avira documentation of a Smart Chat side panel or any other AI assistant. Avira may share the Gen Digital codebase, so this is a conservative value.

brave.models: user's choice: Brave-hosted Qwen, Llama, Claude Haiku/Sonnet/Opus (Premium), or bring your own incl. local Ollama
brave.note: Leo is a private, page-aware assistant in the sidebar and address bar, with Skills and bring-your-own-model support. Leo AI browsing (an agent in an isolated profile) is only an opt-in early test behind a feature flag in all channels, so it isn't counted as a shipped agent. Leo can be turned off in settings or by policy.

brave-origin.note: Origin is the stripped edition of Brave ($59.99 once, free on Linux) that removes extras like Leo AI by default. If you use it as an upgrade to regular Brave, you can switch features back on individually.

browseros.models: rate-limited default model, bring your own key, or Ollama/LM Studio; neo variant: external agents (Claude Code, Codex, MCP)
browseros.note: The main BrowserOS build has a built-in agent that clicks, navigates and fills forms. It ships with a rate-limited default model or uses your own keys or local models, which need 15K+ tokens of context. A separate BrowserOS neo build is a second browser driven by external MCP agents. HN and XDA readers like it as an open AGPL alternative to Comet, but whether you can fully switch off the AI UI is not documented.

chatgpt-atlas.note: Atlas had an Ask ChatGPT sidebar, browser memories, and an agent mode (Plus/Pro/Business only) that could navigate and act. Researchers quickly found prompt injections (omnibox jailbreak, memory poisoning). It is discontinued: OpenAI shut it down on Aug 9 2026, so none of this is usable any more.

comet.note: The tab-aware Comet Assistant handles research, summaries and @tab context. Its agent mode can navigate and fill forms, is free, and now asks permission before acting. Paid Perplexity tiers give higher limits. It is the most capable agent in tests, but Brave and LayerX (CometJacking) showed repeated prompt-injection data exfiltration, and an audit found errors in its summaries.

crest.models: none built in (external coding agents can use allowed Spaces)
crest.note: There is no built-in assistant. Coding agents you run yourself can be allowed to drive specific Spaces, and page translation runs on-device. It is early access and its security has not been independently audited.

cursed-browser.models: a vision LLM (not specified in README)
cursed-browser.note: This is a satirical open-source project in which a vision LLM reads a page's HTML and hallucinates an image of it instead of rendering it. The AI is the rendering engine, so it cannot be turned off. It is not an assistant and has no chat, page help or agent.

dia.models: Claude Opus 4.8 (vendor-hosted; paid AI plans added Aug 2026)
dia.note: The address bar and sidebar assistant can chat with several tabs, write drafts, and run Skills and connectors (Slack, Gmail, Notion). Reviewers rate it polished, but it does not click or fill forms for you. An agentic version was promised for fall 2026 but had not shipped as of Nov 1 2026. Akamai published prompt-injection research on Dia, and the omnibox auto-routes queries to the AI.

duckduckgo.models: user's choice: Claude Haiku 5.5, GPT-5.4 mini, Mistral Small 4, gpt-oss, Gemma; subscribers get Claude Sonnet/Opus 5.5, GPT-5.6
duckduckgo.note: Duck.ai is a private, anonymized chat with a search/AI toggle and a button that summarizes or answers questions about the current page. It doesn't work across tabs or act for you. One toggle in Settings > AI Features turns Duck.ai off completely.

ecosia-browser.models: small open Mistral models hosted in Europe
ecosia-browser.note: The AI comes from Ecosia Search (AI Overviews and AI Chat), not from a browser assistant that's aware of your pages or tabs. Since July 2026 a single 'AI-free search' setting turns it all off.

epic-privacy-browser.note: Epic's official feature pages list tracker/ad blocking and an encrypted proxy, with no built-in AI assistant.

facet.models: Apple Intelligence (on-device) or bring your own AI, any provider
facet.note: Agents in the sidebar work in your tabs, plus AI Peek summaries, Ask all tabs, Gist, voice commands and Sweep. Unlimited agents need the paid Founder tier, so the free tier is limited. First-run setup lets you turn AI completely off. There are very few independent reviews of the AI's quality.

fellou.models: Fellou cloud (vendor models, not disclosed); Eko framework for custom agents
fellou.note: Deep Action plans multi-step tasks across sites and apps, and you can edit the plan before it runs. Deep Search, scheduled tasks and Computer Use are also included. It runs on credits: the free tier covers about 4 tasks and paid plans cost $19-$199/mo. Testers report loops and unreliable runs, and Brave and LayerX showed it was vulnerable to prompt injection.

firefox.models: user's choice: sidebar chatbots (Claude, ChatGPT, Copilot, Gemini, Le Chat); Smart Window models incl. Mistral, or bring your own (local OK)
firefox.note: Smart Window is an opt-in beta (US/Canada/France, Mozilla account needed) whose assistant works with tabs and history, suggests form fills from chosen tabs and watches pages. It never submits forms itself. The 'Block AI enhancements' switch in AI Controls (Firefox 148+) turns off all current and future AI features. Translations and some features run on-device.

floorp.note: Floorp has no assistant of its own. It offers an MCP server so outside AI tools can control it, and may inherit Firefox's optional AI plumbing (I didn't confirm what it exposes), but no AI UI is advertised.

google-chrome.note: Gemini in Chrome has a persistent side panel that sees pages and tabs, plus address-bar AI Mode and writing help. Auto browse, which clicks, types and fills forms for you, is limited to paid Google AI Pro/Ultra subscribers in the US on English desktop Chrome.

helium.note: Helium is built on ungoogled-chromium and explicitly ships with no AI, no account and no telemetry.

island.models: organization's choice: ChatGPT, Copilot, Gemini, Claude, Grok or own model
island.note: Island's Enterprise AI Browser puts the admin's chosen AI in the sidebar with page and company context, and can run governed agent actions in the browser or through Island-hosted MCP. It's enterprise-only: admins enable and restrict everything (paid licenses), and there's no consumer tier. Agent features are enterprise-only and enabled by admins.

microsoft-edge.note: In May 2026 Microsoft retired Copilot Mode and moved its features (reasoning across tabs, Journeys, voice/vision, writing help) into standard Edge. The agent, Browse with Copilot (formerly Copilot Actions), is only for US Microsoft 365 Premium subscribers, plus a business preview limited to admin-allowed sites.

midori.note: Midori's feature list has ad/tracker blocking, an 'IA Shield' protection layer, AstianGO search and MidoriVPN, but no AI assistant.

naver-whale.models: own HyperCLOVA X (Naver AI); ChatGPT/Claude address-bar shortcuts
naver-whale.note: Whale 5 (Oct 2026) officially added AI Chat in the sidebar. It summarizes, translates and answers questions about the current page or chosen tabs, organizes tabs and manages Naver Calendar events after asking for confirmation. Naver AI Briefing is in Quick Search. It doesn't drive arbitrary websites.

norton-neo.note: An AI-native browser with an always-present sidebar assistant, AI search and answers on the new-tab Workspace, writing help in text boxes, link-preview summaries and automatic tab grouping. Reviews say it doesn't click through sites for you, and user reviews are lukewarm about the AI and its unnamed model.

norton-private-browser.note: The side panel, shown by default, includes Gen Digital's Smart Chat for questions and current-page summaries. That's basic chat with no awareness of other tabs.

opera.models: Opera AI (OpenAI + Google Gemini models); ChatGPT and Gemini in sidebar; local Gemma via Web AI preview
opera.note: Opera AI is free with no account, replaced Aria, and understands the current tab or tab group. Browser Connector (MCP) lets outside AI such as ChatGPT or Claude work with live tabs, but agentic browsing as Opera's own feature now lives in Neon. Local Web AI models are an opt-in early preview (Oct 2026).

opera-air.note: Air ships the same free, context-aware Opera AI as Opera One. Whether Air has the same Gemini sidebar entry and local AI controls isn't confirmed.

opera-gx.note: GX has the same free, no-account Opera AI as Opera One, and Browser Connector (MCP) for outside AI clients. Local Web AI models are announced for GX but follow Opera One, so they aren't counted yet.

opera-neon.models: user's choice: OpenAI, Anthropic, Google (Gemini 3 Pro)
opera-neon.note: Opera's AI-native browser with Chat, Do (an agent that browses and fills forms), Make, deep research, scheduled Tasks and an MCP Connector. Downloading is free, but the agents need the $19.90/month Standard plan.

orion.note: Kagi deliberately ships no built-in AI in Orion and cites security research on agent risks. Kagi Assistant is a separate web product.

phi.models: Phi Cloud (default, account needed) or local models via LM Studio/Ollama
phi.note: It has a proactive agent that clicks, types and navigates, keeps an action log, and adds memory stored in a readable local file, scheduled tasks and self-built skills. AI can be switched off entirely. Reviewers call the AI optional, but OpenHunts caught Phi Cloud claiming it had made a CSS change it never made. Whether the AI UI shows by default is unclear, so the conservative value is used.

safari.models: on-device Apple Intelligence (+ Private Cloud Compute)
safari.note: Apple Intelligence adds page summaries, optional automatic tab grouping by topic, Notify Me page-change alerts and extensions built from a description in macOS 27. Safari has no chat assistant or web agent; turning off Apple Intelligence removes all of it. onByDefault assumes Apple Intelligence is left on at setup.

sigmaos.models: OpenAI GPT-4o (Airis); Perplexity/ChatGPT Search selectable for Look it up
sigmaos.note: The Airis companion chats with the current page, explains selected text, simplifies pages into summaries and does web lookups, with no multi-tab or agent features. It is effectively abandoned: there has been no release since early 2025.

strawberry.note: Agents (companions) act in your logged-in tabs, split big jobs into sub-agents, run on schedules and pause for approval before sending or changing things. Free plan has 500 credits a month; paid plans from $20. Benchmarks so far are vendor-run.

ulaa.models: none confirmed (Zoho Zia mentioned for signed-in users)
ulaa.note: I found no official Zoho source for a generative AI assistant in Ulaa. One third-party review mentions optional Zia features for tab organization and phishing detection when signed in, but it's unverified, so I picked the conservative value.

vivaldi.note: Vivaldi publicly refuses to build LLM features such as chat, summaries or agents into the browser, and restated that stance with 7.8 in 2026.

wavebox.models: GPT-5 mini included (Pro); OpenAI/Anthropic via own key; local Ollama or Brainbox Local AI
wavebox.note: Brainbox is a built-in side panel that chats with any tab, including tabs in other Spaces you @-mention. It has writing Skills (reply, rewrite, tone, grammar) and a settings chat that can change Wavebox itself. Pro includes 1M OpenAI tokens a month. It doesn't act on websites.

wren.note: No AI features are listed for the 0.8.0 beta; it positions itself as a small browser that never sends your browsing anywhere.

yab.models: your own Claude or ChatGPT plan; Claude Code/Codex/Cursor via MCP
yab.note: Your own Claude or ChatGPT account clicks, types and reads in your tabs while signed in as you. It asks before sending or paying, and also runs scheduled checks and self-updating folders. OpenHunts lists the AI as optional and it needs your existing plan. Arc users praise it, but there are few independent tests of the agent, and it is still at v0.39.

yandex-browser.note: Alice AI is in the smart bar and a SplitView chat that understands the open page, PDF or video. Yandex has promised Alice AI agents that fill forms and book things, but I couldn't confirm a shipped web agent in the desktop browser, so agent is set to false.

zen-browser.note: Zen hides Firefox's AI chatbot sidebar by default, and tech press lists it as a Firefox alternative without AI. The inherited Firefox code can still be switched on through about:config.
